from.place: For general n=prod_i ell_i^{e_i}, the closed subgroup schemes A[ell_i^{e_i}] have coprime orders, so A[n]=A[ell_1^{e_1}] x ... x A[ell_r^{e_r}] as group schemes (by Bezout's identity the multiplication maps give the direct product decomposition).

title: Coprime torsion decomposition of a module
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, S a finite set of indices, and q : S \to R a family that is pairwise coprime. If every element of M is annihilated by the product of the q i, then the submodules of elements annihilated by q i form an internal direct sum decomposition of M ([def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]).
